summary: Reimplemented Exomiser's hiPHIVE human-only phenotype-matching algorithm in pure Python — no Java virtual machine, under 100 MB of reference data — to rank all 5,267 HPO (Human Phenotype Ontology, a standard vocabulary and graph of clinical features)-annotated genes by how well their curated symptom list matches the child's own HPO terms, without ever reading the panel, the callset or a variant. On the child's own 7 terms (excluding a parental-only term), BUB1B ranks 6th of 5,267, and independently 26th of 18,882 in the unrelated tool Phen2Gene. Joining this ranking to step 2's genome-wide biallelic gene table confirms BUB1B is the best-ranked of the 65 genes carrying a candidate biallelic (two rare protein-altering alleles) set — the next-best is HSPG2, at rank 150.
why: Every candidate found so far came through an eight-gene panel picked by hand from known Mosaic Variegated Aneuploidy biology, which is a circular prior. A phenotype ranking driven only by the child's symptoms is the one check that cannot inherit that bias, because it never sees the panel or the DNA. Without it, agreement between the panel and the DNA proves nothing — it would just be the same assumption checked against itself.
verdict: H005 supported, committed at 0.80: BUB1B is first by phenotype rank among genome-wide biallelic candidates, far ahead of the runner-up. H002 supported at 0.86: the parental term HP:0200067 (recurrent spontaneous abortion) does not belong in the child's own term set — every panel gene, BUB1B included, ranks better without it. H001 stays proposed, its prediction conditioned on the oracle.

inherits.what: step 2's genome-wide gene_biallelic table is what the ranking is joined against for the confirmatory test (H005); the ranking itself needs only public HPO files and ran before step 2 finished, but the cross-check that could have refuted it needed step 2's output to exist.

hands_to.what: H005 and H001 are both settled together by the oracle's reply — a confirmed BUB1B pair makes both predictions observed — and that reply is what step 6 spends its first submission on.

figures.name: track1-gene-scatter.png
figures.reads: One point per gene with a candidate biallelic set (65 genes). X-axis: phenotype rank on the child's own HPO terms, logarithmic, with uncurated genes parked past a labelled boundary at the far right. Y-axis: count of rare protein-altering alleles in the gene. Filled markers are biallelic on PASS calls; hollow markers are biallelic only if a filtered call is rescued. BUB1B is drawn larger and green; genes with a ClinVar pathogenic/likely-pathogenic allele are yellow; other PASS-biallelic genes are blue; rescue-only genes are grey. A dotted vertical line marks phenotype rank 30.
figures.means: Shows two independent instruments — the DNA-derived candidate list on the y-axis, the symptom-derived rank on the x-axis — agreeing on one gene: BUB1B sits alone, far left of every other candidate and left of the rank-30 marker, while the next curated biallelic gene (HSPG2) sits at rank 150.
